titulo: High in fibre, low in salt
intro: How to read a label and talk about what we eat and what state it is in.
p.alimento.consejo: It is more technical than «comida» and common on labels and on TV.
p.rico en.consejo: After «en» comes what it contains: «rico en hierro». It agrees: «ricos en fibra».
p.bajo en.consejo: The opposite of «rico en»: «bajo en sal», «baja en grasas». It changes with gender.
p.conservante.consejo: Careful: English «preservative» is «conservante». «Preservativo» is something very different.
p.colorante.consejo: It comes from «color». On labels it goes next to «conservante»: «sin colorantes».
p.caducado.consejo: It is said of food and of documents: «un yogur caducado», «un carné caducado».
p.podrido.consejo: It comes from «pudrirse». It is said of fruit, vegetables or meat: «una manzana podrida».
p.legumbres.consejo: Almost always plural. They are not vegetables: «lentejas», «garbanzos» and «judías».
p.frutos secos.consejo: It is almost always plural: «un puñado de frutos secos».
p.marisco.consejo: It does not include fish: menus say «pescados y mariscos».
p.integral.consejo: It works for masculine and feminine: «pan integral», «harina integral». Only the plural changes.
p.harina.consejo: The h is silent: «a-RI-na». It is made from wheat, corn and other cereals.
p.nutritivo.consejo: It comes from «nutrir», to feed. A nutritious meal gives the body what it needs.
p.digerir.consejo: The e changes: «digiero», «digieres», «digiere». A heavy meal is hard to digest.
b1.texto:
**What it contains.** A food can be **rico en** fibre, vitamins or iron, and **bajo en** salt, sugar or fats. With **sin** you say what it does not contain: **sin conservantes**, **sin colorantes**, **sin gluten**.

**What state it is in.** With **estar**: **está caducado** (it is past its date) and **está podrido** (it has gone bad).

**Ser or estar.** **Es bueno** means it is healthy or of good quality. **Está bueno** means it tastes good.

**Food groups.** **Las legumbres** (lentils, chickpeas), **los frutos secos** (almonds, walnuts) and **el marisco** (prawns, mussels). Bread and flour can be **integrales**.

**False friend.** English «preservative» is **conservante** in Spanish; **preservativo** is something else.
b2.f0.texto: This cereal is high in fibre and low in sugar.
b2.f1.texto: Does it have preservatives or colourings?
b2.f2.texto: The label says it has none.
b2.f3.texto: Check the date before putting it in the trolley.
b2.f4.texto: This milk has been out of date since yesterday.
b2.f6.texto: Let us buy pulses and nuts, which are very nutritious.
b2.f7.texto: I am taking the wholemeal bread and the flour for the cake.
b4.titulo: Rico en, bajo en, sin, and ser or estar
b4.texto:
**Rico en / bajo en + noun.** The adjective agrees with the food: **un yogur bajo en grasa**, **unos cereales ricos en fibra**, **una bebida baja en azúcar**.

**Sin + noun** says what is missing: **sin sal**, **sin conservantes**. It takes no article.

**Ser or estar** changes the meaning of the adjective:

- **Es bueno** / **es malo**: healthy or harmful, of good or bad quality.
- **Está bueno** / **está malo**: it tastes good or it has gone off.

The state of food goes with **estar**: **está caducado**, **está podrido**.
b4.e0.texto: These cereals are high in fibre.
b4.e1.texto: The bread without preservatives tastes very good.
b4.e2.texto: Fresh fish is good for your health.
b5.f0.texto: The neighbourhood market smells of wholemeal bread and toasted flour.
b5.f1.texto: The pulses sleep in cloth sacks and shine like small coloured stones.
b5.f2.texto: A seller stirs the nuts with a wooden scoop.
b5.f3.texto: From the next stall comes the salty smell of the shellfish.
b5.f4.texto: A girl tries an almond and wrinkles her nose at the bitter taste.
b5.f5.texto: A woman calmly reads the label on a jar of jam.
b5.f6.texto: She looks for the expiry date and the list of ingredients.
b5.f7.texto: Her finger stops on the word colorantes, like a bee on a flower.
b5.f8.texto: She puts the jar back on the shelf and chooses another without preservatives.
b5.f9.texto: The sweet smell of ripe fruit goes with her to the exit.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «bajo en» says it has little of something.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That is «rico en sal». «Bajo en» is the opposite.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That would be «sin sal». «Bajo en» allows a little.
b8.frase: Las legumbres son ricas en hierro
b9.o0.refuerzo: That says it is healthy or good quality, not how it tastes.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That says it is out of date, not that it tastes good.
b9.pregunta: Which sentence says it tastes good?
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «caducado» is what is past its date.
b11.o1.refuerzo: It is said of fruit or meat that smells bad, not of the date.
b11.o2.refuerzo: That is said of bread or flour, not of yoghurt.
b11.pregunta: How is a yoghurt that is past its date?
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes: chickpeas, lentils and beans are pulses.
b12.pregunta: Which of these foods is a pulse?
p.cereal.consejo: Stress the last syllable: «se-re-AL». The plural «cereales» is the same word used for many grains.
p.fibra.consejo: «fibra» is stressed on the first syllable, so it is FI-bra. It is a feminine noun, so say «la fibra».
p.conservantes.consejo: Notice the «v» is pronounced «b»: «con-ser-BAN-tes». Think of the word «conservar», to keep.
p.colorantes.consejo: It comes from «color». Here the «o» is open and clear: «ko-lo-RAN-tes».
p.ponerlo.consejo: The pronoun «lo» attaches to the infinitive: «poner» + «lo» = «ponerlo».
p.caducada.consejo: It is the feminine form of «caducado», so it agrees with a feminine noun such as «la leche».
p.podridas.consejo: «podrida» means rotten; the plural form «podridas» agrees with «fresas».
p.compremos.consejo: The «-emos» ending here means «let us». Compare «compramos» (we buy).
p.nutritivos.consejo: Say it with the stress on «TI»: «nu-tri-TI-vos». It comes from «nutrir», to nourish.
p.cereales.consejo: The plural «cereales» keeps the same sound as the singular, only with an «-es» at the end.
p.ricos.consejo: «rico» means rich or tasty. Use «ricos» when the noun is masculine plural.
p.tostada.consejo: «tostada» agrees with the feminine noun «harina». It comes from «tostar», to toast.
p.sacos.consejo: «saco» is a large bag. Its stress is on the first syllable: SA-kos.
p.pala.consejo: «pala» is feminine: «la pala». Note that «palo» is a stick, a different word.
p.almendra.consejo: The «d» between vowels is soft: «al-MEN-dra». The stress is on «MEN».
p.sabor.consejo: «sabor» is masculine and has the stress at the end: sa-BOR. Note «saber» is to know, not to taste.
p.bote.consejo: «bote» is masculine: «el bote». The stress is on «BO»: BO-te.
p.caducidad.consejo: The «z» and «c» before «i» sound like «th» in Spain: «ka-du-thi-DAD».
p.abeja.consejo: «abeja» is feminine: «la abeja». The «j» sounds like a strong «h» in Spanish: a-BE-ha.
p.flor.consejo: «flor» is feminine: «la flor». Its stress is on the only syllable: FLOR.
p.poca.consejo: «poca» agrees with a feminine noun, like «poca sal». Use «poco» with masculine nouns.
p.garbanzos.consejo: «garbanzos» is masculine plural: «los garbanzos». Pronounce the «z» as «th» in Spain.
